_comment: Curated, real, geographically diverse flood/wetland-significant locations for VAMIKA's pre-seeded instant-demo cache (Tier 1). Coordinates are approximate region centers, not tied to any specific historical event date - the pre-seed script queries NASA CMR for whatever real NISAR acquisitions actually exist at each place and picks the best available real before/after pair. This list is version-controlled; backend/data/featured_cache.json (generated by the pre-seed script) holds the per-location analysis linkage and is NOT version-controlled.

locations.name: Sundarbans
locations.blurb: The world's largest mangrove forest and a UNESCO World Heritage site, forming a critical natural flood buffer for the Ganges-Brahmaputra delta.

locations.name: Pantanal
locations.blurb: The world's largest tropical wetland, spanning Brazil, Bolivia and Paraguay, with an extreme seasonal flood pulse that drives one of the planet's richest concentrations of wildlife.

locations.name: Mississippi River Delta
locations.blurb: Louisiana's rapidly eroding coastal wetlands near New Orleans, repeatedly reshaped by hurricane storm-surge flooding.

locations.name: Okavango Delta
locations.blurb: A UNESCO World Heritage inland river delta in the Kalahari Desert that floods seasonally, supporting an exceptional concentration of wildlife in an otherwise arid region.

locations.name: Amazon Floodplain (Iquitos)
locations.blurb: Seasonally-flooded Amazon varzea forest, where L-band SAR can see standing water beneath the forest canopy that optical satellites cannot.

locations.name: Po River Delta
locations.blurb: The Mediterranean's largest wetland and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, at the mouth of Italy's longest river.

locations.name: Danube Delta
locations.blurb: Europe's best-preserved river delta and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, with extensive seasonal floodplain wetlands.

locations.name: Majuli Island (Brahmaputra)
locations.blurb: The world's largest river island, on the Brahmaputra in Assam, which loses significant land to annual monsoon flooding and erosion.

locations.name: Mekong Delta
locations.blurb: Vietnam's 'rice bowl', home to roughly 17 million people, where annual monsoon flooding is both an agricultural lifeline and a recurring hazard.

locations.name: Tonle Sap Lake
locations.blurb: Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake, unique for reversing its flow direction each monsoon season and expanding to several times its dry-season size.

locations.name: Poyang Lake
locations.blurb: China's largest freshwater lake, with one of the most extreme seasonal area variations of any lake on Earth.

locations.name: Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta (Dhaka)
locations.blurb: The world's largest river delta, home to one of the most densely-populated and flood-exposed regions on the planet.

locations.name: Irrawaddy Delta
locations.blurb: A low-lying rice-growing delta devastated by catastrophic storm-surge flooding during Cyclone Nargis in 2008.

locations.name: Jakarta
locations.blurb: A megacity facing chronic monsoon and tidal flooding, worsened by rapid land subsidence.

locations.name: Indus River Floodplain (Sindh)
locations.blurb: The lower Indus floodplain, site of Pakistan's catastrophic 2022 floods that submerged roughly a third of the country at their peak.

locations.name: Inner Niger Delta
locations.blurb: A vast Sahelian floodplain wetland that seasonally inundates to support fishing, farming and grazing for millions of people.

locations.name: Lake Chad Basin
locations.blurb: A dramatically shrinking Sahelian lake whose remaining wetlands and seasonal floodplains support millions across four countries.

locations.name: Everglades
locations.blurb: The largest subtropical wetland in the United States, a unique 'river of grass' ecosystem shaped by seasonal flooding.

locations.name: Barotse Floodplain (Zambezi)
locations.blurb: A UNESCO-listed Zambezi River floodplain whose annual flood pulse drives the traditional Kuomboka ceremony and local livelihoods.

locations.name: Kakadu Wetlands
locations.blurb: A UNESCO World Heritage monsoonal floodplain in Australia's Northern Territory, among the most biodiverse wetlands on Earth.

locations.name: Wadden Sea
locations.blurb: The world's largest unbroken system of intertidal sand and mud flats, a UNESCO World Heritage site along the North Sea coast.

locations.name: Venice Lagoon
locations.blurb: Venice's historic lagoon, increasingly affected by 'Acqua Alta' tidal flooding events.

locations.name: Houston / Texas Gulf Coast
locations.blurb: A major US metropolitan area catastrophically flooded by Hurricane Harvey's record rainfall in 2017.

locations.name: Esteros del Ibera
locations.blurb: South America's second-largest wetland after the Pantanal, a vast marshland system in northeastern Argentina.

locations.name: Camargue
locations.blurb: The Rhone River delta's wetlands on the Mediterranean coast, famed for their flamingos and seasonal flooding.
